# Real-time approximations

Also called: Real-time volumetric global illumination, Approximate volumetric light transport

## Overview
Real-time approximations estimate [light transport in participating media](#32-light-transport-in-participating-media.md) within strict latency budgets, avoiding the prohibitive cost of full path tracing or iterative radiative transfer equation (RTE) solvers [G]. They set themselves apart from sibling methods like [Optical models](33-optical-models.md) by prioritizing computational efficiency and dynamic scene support over physical accuracy, and from [Local illumination, shadows and ambient occlusion](34-local-illumination-shadows-and-ambient-occlusion.md) by explicitly handling indirect scattering and global illumination effects in volumes [G].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the goal of approximating the integral of the radiative transfer equation for multiple scattering orders without solving it iteratively per frame [G]. They typically rely on one or more of the following mechanisms:
1. **Spatial Discretization:** The volume is discretized into a structured grid (voxels, froxels) or a hierarchical structure (octrees, light volumes) to allow efficient spatial queries and interpolation [G].
2. **Precomputation or Caching:** Lighting information (attenuation, visibility, or flux) is precomputed offline or updated incrementally per frame, stored in textures or data structures, and queried at runtime [G].
3. **Dimensionality Reduction:** Directional information is compressed using basis functions (e.g., [Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)) or approximated using geometric primitives (e.g., cones, light volumes with blur widths) to reduce the cost of evaluating the scattering integral [G].
4. **Temporal Stability:** Many methods incorporate [temporal accumulation](#2080-temporal-accumulation-closest-hit.md) (e.g., TAA reprojection) to stabilize noise and reduce per-frame computational load [G].

## Subtopics

### [Multiple Scattering Approximation via Light Volume Lookup](1188-multiple-scattering-approximation-via-light-volume-lookup.md)
Approximates multiple scattering by precomputing light attenuation into a volumetric data structure (the "light volume") and treating the multiple scattering contribution as a lookup operation based on accumulated optical thickness and a derived blurring width [1188-multiple-scattering-approximation-via-light-volume-lookup.md]. It solves the problem of expensive numerical integration of the RTE for multiple scattering orders by replacing it with a spatially varying blur lookup, allowing for near-real-time rendering of complex volumetric effects like smoke and clouds [1188-multiple-scattering-approximation-via-light-volume-lookup.md]. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) by explicitly modeling the spatial spreading of light beams through the medium using a derived width parameter, rather than relying on [cone tracing](#5679-cone-tracing.md) or [spherical harmonics for visibility approximation](#6294-spherical-harmonics-ao.md) [1188-multiple-scattering-approximation-via-light-volume-lookup.md]. Choose it when rendering heterogeneous media with strong multiple scattering where cone tracing fails to capture beam spread.

### [Spherical Harmonic Volumetric Visibility](1225-spherical-harmonic-volumetric-visibility.md)
A real-time dynamic lighting technique for [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) that encodes local and global volumetric visibility using [spherical harmonic basis](#4390-spherical-harmonics-encoder.md) functions [1225-spherical-harmonic-volumetric-visibility.md]. It sets itself apart from its siblings by storing these coefficients in a multiresolution grid to handle directional lights, point lights, and environment maps efficiently [1225-spherical-harmonic-volumetric-visibility.md]. Unlike [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) which relies on geometric cone tracing, or [Froxel-based Volumetric Rendering](1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md) which uses hierarchical voxel blocks, this method projects visibility into a frequency domain to approximate scattering integrals [1225-spherical-harmonic-volumetric-visibility.md]. Choose it when [directional lighting](#2790-volpack-lighting-setup.md) accuracy and smooth interpolation across varying densities are prioritized over spatially explicit cone tracing.

### [Modular Transfer](1249-modular-transfer.md)
A precomputation-based rendering technique for volumetric media with repeated structures, such as fabrics and wood, that approximates high-order multiple scattering by modularly combining precomputed flux transfer matrices for exemplar blocks [1249-modular-transfer.md]. It solves the problem of rendering complex, optically thick media with anisotropic scattering by splitting light transport paths into components precomputed offline and computed at runtime, making path integrals separable via isotropy and diffuser events [1249-modular-transfer.md]. Unlike its siblings, MFT uses flux instead of light fields to address the curse of dimensionality, avoiding the massive storage overhead of directional discretizations [1249-modular-transfer.md]. It builds on [Real-time approximations](36-real-time-approximations.md) by providing a scalable alternative to [voxel cone tracing](#1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) and froxels for heterogeneous media where [diffusion approximations](#2372-diffusion-approximation.md) fail due to strong heterogeneity and anisotropy [1249-modular-transfer.md]. Choose it for structured, optically thick media where traditional voxel methods suffer from storage or computational bottlenecks.

### [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md)
A real-time global illumination technique that approximates indirect diffuse and specular lighting by voxelizing the scene geometry into a 3D texture or sparse octree and tracing cones through this volume to accumulate radiance [1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md]. It solves the problem of computing indirect light (interreflections) in dynamic scenes where precomputed methods are infeasible and full ray tracing is too slow [1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md]. Unlike [Spherical Harmonic Volumetric Visibility](1225-spherical-harmonic-volumetric-visibility.md) which encodes lighting in frequency domain, or [Precomputed Lighting (Baking)](2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md) which requires static geometry, VCT operates on a spatially explicit voxel representation, allowing for dynamic objects and view-dependent effects like soft shadows and glossy reflections [1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md]. Choose it for dynamic scenes requiring view-dependent indirect lighting and soft shadows without baking.

### [Froxel-based Volumetric Rendering](1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md)
A real-time approximation for light transport in participating media that amortizes ray-queried occlusion lighting work by dividing the camera view frustum into a 3D grid of voxels ("froxels") [1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md]. It solves the high computational cost of per-pixel [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) by collapsing per-pixel fog cost to a fixed march in an integrate pass, delivering spatial-accumulation savings [1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md]. Unlike [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) which relies on cone tracing for indirect lighting, or [Precomputed Lighting (Baking)](2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md) which uses static data, this method computes dynamic in-scattered radiance and shadows per froxel, often combined with [Froxel TAA Reprojection](1920-froxel-taa-reprojection.md) to stabilize temporal noise [1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md]. Choose it for large-scale [atmospheric fog](#4400-height-based-fog-with-directional-in-scatter.md) and volumetric effects where per-pixel ray marching is too expensive.

### [Precomputed Lighting (Baking)](2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md)
A technique to accelerate volumetric rendering by pre-computing the lighting term ($L_i$) and storing it in the grid's voxels, allowing the renderer to skip evaluating $L_i$ at each raymarching step on the camera ray [2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md]. It approximates volumetric shadows by precalculating illumination for each voxel center, enabling trilinear interpolation at render time [2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md]. Unlike [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) which computes lighting dynamically during traversal, this method is view-independent but scene and light source dependent [2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md]. Choose it for static scenes or environments where lighting changes infrequently, allowing significant runtime savings at the cost of re-baking overhead.

### [Hardware Ray Tracing Global Illumination](3648-hardware-ray-tracing-global-illumination.md)
Approximates one-bounce diffuse global illumination by cosine-sampling the hemisphere around a surface normal, tracing short rays via hardware RT cores, and [gathering](#9569-gathering.md) indirect irradiance from hits or skylight if rays escape [3648-hardware-ray-tracing-global-illumination.md]. It differs from sibling methods like Voxel Cone Tracing by using explicit ray queries against [voxel bricks](#5794-voxel-bricks.md) rather than cone-based approximations, and from [Precomputed Lighting](#2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md) by computing the indirect term per-frame rather than baking it offline [3648-hardware-ray-tracing-global-illumination.md]. Choose it when hardware RT cores are available and explicit ray queries against voxel structures are preferred over cone tracing.

### [Reflection Probes](4344-reflection-probes.md)
Approximates incoming radiance by storing sparse environment maps at specific locations in the scene, trading spatial precision for high angular resolution [4344-reflection-probes.md]. Unlike precomputed lighting methods that bake static data, [reflection probes](#4344-reflection-probes.md) can be updated dynamically, allowing them to capture dynamic global illumination effects [4344-reflection-probes.md]. They differ from voxel-based methods like Voxel Cone Tracing by storing full-resolution directional radiance rather than compressed scattering data, making them suitable for accurate surface reflections but less effective for volumetric [scattering integration](#5367-in-scattering-model.md) [4344-reflection-probes.md]. Choose them for scenes requiring accurate surface reflections and dynamic environment updates without full volumetric integration.

### [Volumetric Light Scattering via Froxel Clustering](4460-volumetric-light-scattering-via-froxel-clustering.md)
A rendering technique that computes volumetric light scattering for local lights (point and spot) within a fog volume by evaluating light contributions at froxel midpoints using clustered light lists, skipping the sun and non-volumetric lights [4460-volumetric-light-scattering-via-froxel-clustering.md]. It differs from [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) by avoiding ray marching through the volume for scattering, instead relying on pre-clustered light lists and a single sample per light per froxel, and from [Froxel-based Volumetric Rendering](1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md) by specifically targeting local light scattering rather than general volume [density rendering](#2421-density-activation.md). Choose it for scenes with many local lights where clustered evaluation reduces per-froxel shading cost.

### [Deferred Voxel Shading](4685-deferred-voxel-shading.md)
A real-time global illumination technique that merges voxel cone tracing with deferred shading to approximate indirect lighting effects such as diffuse/specular reflections, color bleeding, emissive materials, and ambient occlusion [4685-deferred-voxel-shading.md]. Unlike forward voxel cone tracing, which computes lighting per fragment during geometry rendering, this method delays lighting calculations to a post-processing stage, avoiding redundant computations for overlapping polygons and enhancing performance in scenes with many light sources [4685-deferred-voxel-shading.md]. It builds on [Real-time approximations](36-real-time-approximations.md) by utilizing spatial discretization and precomputed voxel structures to evaluate the radiative transfer equation efficiently [4685-deferred-voxel-shading.md]. Choose it for deferred rendering pipelines where indirect lighting and shadows are needed without forward shading overhead.

#### Modular Cell PRT
Utilize modular cells to precompute transfer, stitching multiple unit cells together and warping them to approximate scene geometry [S1, unofficial]. Propagate radiance first to cell borders acting as interfaces, then to neighboring cells using precomputed models [S1, unofficial].

## Background
Real-time approximations for volumetric rendering emerged as hardware capabilities improved, allowing for more complex lighting calculations within frame budgets [G]. Early approaches relied on precomputed lighting (baking) [2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md] [G]. The introduction of voxel-based techniques like Voxel Cone Tracing [1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md] and Froxel-based methods [1919-froxel-based-volumetric-rendering.md] enabled dynamic global illumination in participating media [G]. More recent methods, such as [Modular Transfer](#1249-modular-transfer.md) [1249-modular-transfer.md] and Light Volume Lookup [1188-multiple-scattering-approximation-via-light-volume-lookup.md], focus on specific types of media (e.g., structured fabrics, smoke) and use advanced precomputation and approximation strategies to handle multiple scattering efficiently [G]. The field continues to evolve with the integration of hardware ray tracing [3648-hardware-ray-tracing-global-illumination.md] and machine learning techniques [G].
